title: Hold The Line Open
subject: a long-distance call
caption: An indie rock band recorded live in one room — drums, bass and two electric guitars, one clean and arpeggiated, one with light overdrive. A raspy male voice sings close-miked and conversational in the verses and pushes into a shout on the chorus. Bone-dry drums with audible room bleed, no reverb on the vocal, tape saturation on the bus. Driving, 132 BPM, E minor. Urgent, unresolved.
lyrics:
[Intro - Guitars]

[Verse 1]
Eight hours and a bad connection
You say my name and then it cuts
I hold the phone against the window
Like the glass could help somehow

[Pre-Chorus]
Don't hang up yet
Don't hang up yet

[Chorus]
Hold the line open
Even if there's nothing on it
I'd rather hear you breathing wrong
Than hear the room without you in it

[Verse 2]
You're asleep before my morning
I'm asleep before your night
We trade the same four hours over
Like they're all we're allowed

[Guitar Solo]

[Bridge]
I counted every time it dropped
I stopped at forty-one
I kept redialing anyway

[Chorus]
Hold the line open
Even if there's nothing on it
I'd rather hear you breathing wrong
Than hear the room without you in it

[Outro]
Still here
Still here
